subject: science
passage: Rooibos, a reddish herbal tea popular in South Africa and increasingly around the world, is made from the needle-like leaves of a shrub that grows wild in only one place. The dry, sandy slopes of the Cederberg Mountains north of Cape ______ the plant the particular soil and climate it needs, and attempts to farm it elsewhere have largely failed.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject of the second sentence is "The dry, sandy slopes of the Cederberg Mountains north of Cape Town," and its verb is "give." No punctuation should separate a subject from its verb, even when the subject is long, so nothing goes between "Town" and "give."
explanation.A: Incorrect. A semicolon joins two independent clauses; here it would cut the subject off from its verb.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A single dash sets off extra information at the end of a sentence; it can't separate a subject from its verb.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A single comma can't separate a subject from its verb.
explanation.D: Correct. The long subject "The dry, sandy slopes … north of Cape Town" flows straight into its verb "give" with no punctuation.
